rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those attached to worldly life and heedless of God's signs are blind to the Hereafter and face Hell as requital.
rows.anchor: continue to be blind and deaf and do not have the fear of the Hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word rajāʾ carries its ordinary, literal sense of hope.
rows.anchor: The word رﺟﺎءhere means “hope” and this is its real meaning too.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's guidance of believers means leading them to the destination that fulfills the purpose of creation.
rows.anchor: The word “guide” here means to guide people to reach the destination which is the purpose of creation of all the universe.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God assigns the believers their rank and status according to their deeds.
rows.anchor: God will guide them to their rank and status in accordance with their deeds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers' praise expresses their joy that the universe has a real purpose rather than being mere amusement.
rows.anchor: Their exclamation in return expresses their jubilation that their contention that this universe has a purpose

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers congratulate one another on success, while the disbelievers are doomed and curse one another.
rows.anchor: They will congratulate one another on this success. On the other hand, the disbelievers will be doomed and will curse one another.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers ask why punishment is not shown as a sample; God's established practice begins with mercy and delays anger, or their case would have ended long ago.
rows.anchor: His established practice is that He takes initiative in mercy; He is very slow to show anger.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who demand punishment cry out when seized, grow arrogant if reprieved, and refuse guidance in any event.
rows.anchor: when they are seized by God, they start to raise a hue and cry. Then if they are given respite, they again start showing arrogance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The audience should learn from past nations they succeeded, since their own fate will be no different.
rows.anchor: seek a lesson from the nations of the past – nations whom they succeeded

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponents demand a replacement or alteration of the Qur'an to suit them because they reject its monotheism and warning of punishment.
rows.anchor: They wanted the Qur’ ān to be totally changed or altered as much so that it suited them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet has no authority to change revelation; he is carrying out a responsibility from God and would not have disclosed it if he could refuse it.
rows.anchor: he does not have the authority to make any change in it. It is a God-given responsibility that he is discharging.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Raʿd is the counterpart of the preceding sūra, Yūsuf, and both share the same basic theme.
rows.anchor: This sūrah is the counterpart of S ūrah Yūsuf, the previous sūrah. There is no basic difference in the theme of both sūrahs.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūras address the conflict between truth and evil after the Qur'an's revelation and identify the group destined to prevail.
rows.anchor: a conflict between truth and evil ensued when the Qur’ ān was revealed. This sūrahs highlights the group which was supposed to succeed ultimately in this conflict.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yūsuf argues through events in Joseph's life, whereas al-Raʿd argues from human intellect and nature.
rows.anchor: in this sūrah, arguments are drawn from human intellect and nature for this purpose

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 17–22 are identified as the sūra's thematic center.
rows.anchor: Verses 17 to 22 highlight the theme of the sūrah.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi rejects the codices' Madinan classification: in his view, the sūra is wholly Makkan, with no Madinan verse.
rows.anchor: Some codices regard it to be Madī nan, which I fail to understand. Not one of its verse is Mad īnan in my opinion

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening addresses the Prophet, affirms the revelation as true and certain, and says most people will remain stubborn and disbelieve.
rows.anchor: these are verses of God’s Book and are not something unfounded. Every statement in it is true

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cosmic signs show that one wise planner governs the universe.
rows.anchor: Those signs of the universe are referred to that show that it is being run by a single wise planner.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universe's vast providence and sustenance reveal a serious purpose that will appear in time, rather than creation for amusement.
rows.anchor: there is a vast system of providence and sustenance in it which shows that its creator has not created it for amusement

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unity amid diversity and harmony amid discord throughout the universe point to one creator and owner.
rows.anchor: unity in diversity and harmony in discord are found in every part of this universe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' astonishment at resurrection amounts to denying God.
rows.anchor: This amazement is tantamount to God’s denial.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their necks are metaphorically fettered, leaving them unable to look up at heavenly signs or down at earthly ones.
rows.anchor: Their necks have been fettered in yokes. They can neither raise their eyes to observe the signs of the heavens

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They demand punishment before repentance despite having history from which to learn.
rows.anchor: They want to hasten the punishment before repentance even though they can learn a lot from history.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's mercy grants respite despite rebellion, but His retribution is severe and no one escapes when He seizes them.
rows.anchor: It is God’s mercy that in spite of the rebelliousness of people, He gives respite to them. However, He is also stern in retribution.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In response to the demand for a punishment sign, the Prophet is told his role is to warn; bringing punishment or setting its time is not his responsibility.
rows.anchor: his only task is to warn people of this punishment. Bringing it or prescribing its time is not his responsibility.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's established practice sends a messenger to every nation with warning and glad tidings; a nation that denies the messenger is necessarily destroyed.
rows.anchor: He sends a messenger to every nation to warn them and to give them glad tidings. If the nation denies it, it is necessarily destroyed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God knows the timing and exact nature of what a pregnant woman will deliver, just as He alone knows the timing and nature of punishment.
rows.anchor: only God its time as well as what exactly she will deliver

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows every deed and thought, whether secret or open and whether done by day or night.
rows.anchor: all their deeds and thoughts are in God’s knowledge whether done secretly or openly – in the light of the day or in the dark of the night.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels appointed by God watch over people.
rows.anchor: Angels deputed by God are overseeing them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can seize people whenever and wherever He wills.
rows.anchor: He can seize them whenever He wants and wherever He wants.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God continues to show a nation favor until its people change their attitude; then unavoidable punishment comes upon it.
rows.anchor: He does not stop showing affection to a nation until it adopts the wrong attitude. When they do this, divine punishment – which none can ward off – visits it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lightning and thunder are visible signs of punishment, and God could destroy people with one lightning bolt, displaying His immense power.
rows.anchor: For example lightning and thunder. God can destroy people with a single bolt of lightning whenever He wants to.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling on anyone besides God resembles chasing a mirage; self-appointed deities and intercessors cannot benefit anyone.
rows.anchor: Invoking someone other than God is like regarding a mirage to be water and then running after it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every object in the universe witnesses to God's oneness, and even people's shadows prostrate to Him.
rows.anchor: Every object of this universe, through its very existence, bears witness to the oneness of God. People whose necks do not bend before God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is futile to call beings that lack authority to harm or benefit anyone.
rows.anchor: It is futile to call those who do not even have authority to harm or benefit anyone.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheism contradicts God's justice and wisdom because He alone creates and controls all things.
rows.anchor: Polytheism nullifies God’s justice and wisdom. God is the creator of everything and He alone controls everyone.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs illustrate that God preserves what benefits and removes what does not.
rows.anchor: God keeps intact what is beneficial and destroys that is not.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This image assures that God will uproot evil and make truth prevail in the conflict following the Qur'an's revelation and the Prophet's preaching.
rows.anchor: God will root out evil and make the truth prevail.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who accept the Prophet's message and follow God's path are promised success, while those who oppose him are cursed.
rows.anchor: Glad tidings of success are given to those who accept the message of the Prophet (sws) and turn to tread the path of God. Those who opposed his message are cursed.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage answers why worldly wealth and treasures remain with people who vehemently oppose God and His messenger if believers deserve God's favors.
rows.anchor: why have are the wealth and treasures of the world in control of those who vehemently oppose God and His messenger

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' request for a miracle is answered by saying that remembrance of God and reflection on His attributes, rather than a miracle, satisfies hearts.
rows.anchor: what gives satisfaction to the hearts is being reminded of God and His attributes and reflecting on them and not some miracle.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is assured that earlier prophets and messengers faced the same opposition; he should recite God's revealed Book and trust Him.
rows.anchor: what he is facing was also faced by prophets and messengers before him. He should recite out to his people the Book that has been revealed to him by God and trust Him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a Qur'an that moved mountains, shattered the earth, and made the dead speak would not make the disbelievers abandon their stance.
rows.anchor: Even if a Qur’ ān is revealed for them through which mountains start to move, the earth is smashed to pieces and the dead start talking, they will remain adamant on their stance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith is not imposed: had God wanted compulsion, He would have guided everyone to the straight path.
rows.anchor: God has not placed any compulsion in faith. Had He liked compulsion, He would have guided everyone to the straight path.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Signs of punishment will keep appearing nearby until the decisive punishment arrives.
rows.anchor: The signs of punishment will continue to be revealed before them or in surrounding areas until the time of the decisive punishment.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier messengers were mocked too, but God's punishment eventually settled the matter against their mockers.
rows.anchor: earlier messengers were also mocked at. Finally, God’s punishment arrived and decided the matter of the jesters.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheistic deities and intercessors are fabrications; those deceived by them face God's wrath in this world and worse torment in the Hereafter, with no savior.
rows.anchor: These deities and intercessors do not exist. All these are concoctions. Those who are deceived by their souls in this regard will face God’s wrath in this world

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only those who fear God receive the eternal favor of Paradise.
rows.anchor: Only they will receive the eternal favour of Paradise who fear God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among the People of the Book, one group welcomed the Qur'an because it adhered to truth, while another opposed it because of its fabricated religious innovations.
rows.anchor: One of them adhered to the truth and hence welcomed the Qur’ ān will full enthusiasm. The other opposed it because it remained entangled in religious innovations it had fabricated.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's declaration of truth to them is cited, and he is warned that following their innovations after revelation would leave him without protection from God.
rows.anchor: if after the truth being revealed to him by God he follows their innovations, none can save him from God’s grasp.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Previous messengers were human beings like the Prophet, not angels or heavenly creatures, and they had wives.
rows.anchor: all messengers who came before him were not angels or heavenly creatures; they were human beings like him and had wives too like him.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers performed miracles only by God's command, never on their own authority.
rows.anchor: Whatever miracles they showed, they showed at God’s behest and not on their own authority.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may show the opponents some of the warned punishment during the Prophet's life, or take him before they are punished.
rows.anchor: some part of it may be shown to them in his own lifetime by God and this too can happen that he is taken away from this world by God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shrinking borders and impending encirclement show that God is closing in on the opponents and reveal who will ultimately succeed.
rows.anchor: God is moving towards them by reducing their borders and soon they will be surrounded. At that time, they will come to know who succeeded ultimately.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If opponents deny his messengerhood, the Prophet should say that God and those knowledgeable of His Book suffice as witnesses.
rows.anchor: God and those who have knowledge of God’s Book are sufficient witnesses between him and them.

none: Qur'anic text and translation only; no commentary point is stated.
